message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"60b477f10fdb6066007cd5dc556a3561534fc1dab5809b1e87d3be12a9823ff6","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","units":[{"unit_id":"sec03-u01","module_id":"sec03-m01","objective_ids":["sec03-u01"],"title":{"text":"Losing a license, paying back","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A traffic conviction can cost you the license on top of the court's penalty, so the consequences go beyond a fine.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01"]},{"text":"Knowing the reinstatement fees ahead of time shows how expensive a lost license becomes.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Taylor's license is suspended for unpaid child support, and Taylor mails the license back late.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Reinstatement always starts at the base fee of at least one hundred dollars, and each problem adds its own charge.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R09"]},"result":{"text":"Taylor pays at least one hundred dollars, plus fifty for the late surrender and fifty for the child-support suspension.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09","sec03-F03","sec03-F04"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking reinstatement is just one flat fee no matter what happened.","fact_ids":["sec03-R09"]},"correction":{"text":"The base fee is at least one hundred dollars, and a late surrender, a drug conviction or a child-support suspension each add more.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-R09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"One hundred to start, then add the extras.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02","sec03-R09"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver lost the license after a drug-related conviction. What extra amount is added to reinstatement?","fact_ids":["sec03-F04"]},"answer":{"text":"Twenty-five dollars.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04"]},"rationale":{"text":"A drug-related conviction adds twenty-five dollars on top of the base reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When a license is taken","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four ways to lose a license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Fees to get it back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"This chapter is about what can happen to your license when the rules are broken, and this first lesson sets the stage. A conviction for breaking a traffic law can bring a court penalty, but it can also cost you the license itself, through cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification. Getting relicensed afterward is never free. There is a reinstatement fee, and extra charges can pile on top of it. We will also look at cancellation, which is different because it is about whether you were ever entitled to the license in the first place.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The base reinstatement fee","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"At least one hundred dollars.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Plus any other state-law requirements.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Whatever the reason you lost the license, whether a cancellation, a suspension, a revocation or a disqualification, getting relicensed requires a reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars. That is the starting point, not the whole bill, and other requirements set by state law may also apply. Think of the base fee as the price of reopening your record as a licensed driver. The add-on charges we look at next depend on what led to the loss or on how you handled it afterward, so two drivers can pay very different totals.","fact_ids":["sec03-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Charges added on top","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Late surrender: fifty dollars more.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-R09"]},{"text":"Drug conviction: twenty-five. Child support: fifty.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Three extra charges can be added to the reinstatement fee. If you fail to surrender your license within the allowed time after it is canceled, revoked or suspended, a fifty-dollar fee is added. Reinstating after a drug-related conviction costs an extra twenty-five dollars. Reinstating after a suspension for unpaid child support costs an extra fifty dollars. These charges stack, so a driver who surrendered late and was suspended for child support pays the base fee plus fifty plus fifty. Turning the license in on time is one cost you can control.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Cancellation is about entitlement","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Not entitled to the license: cancellation.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F01"]},{"text":"False or missing application information too.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is where learners slip. Cancellation is not a punishment for a bad driving record. The ALEA Director may cancel a license on finding that the holder was not entitled to it in the first place. Missing or false information on the application, or fraud in applying, is also grounds for cancellation. So when a question describes someone who lied on the application, think cancellation. When it describes a serious offense on the road, think revocation or suspension instead. Keeping the reason in mind helps you pick the right word on the test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05","sec03-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the add-on fees","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"What does a drug conviction add?","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver lost the license after a drug-related conviction. What extra amount is added to reinstatement? Settle on your answer first. The answer is twenty-five dollars. That charge sits on top of the base reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars. Do not confuse it with the fifty-dollar charges, which apply to a late license surrender and to a suspension for unpaid child support. If you mixed them up, line the three add-ons up again: late surrender fifty, drug conviction twenty-five, child support fifty.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F02","sec03-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"What losing a license costs","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Court penalty plus license action.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-R09"]},{"text":"Base fee plus any add-ons.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, a traffic conviction can bring cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification of your license on top of what the court imposes. Coming back always costs a reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars, plus fifty for a late surrender, twenty-five after a drug conviction, and fifty after a child-support suspension. Cancellation stands apart, because it happens when the holder was not entitled to the license, including false or missing application information. In the next lesson we look closely at revocation and the offenses that make it mandatory.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u02","module_id":"sec03-m02","objective_ids":["sec03-u02"],"title":{"text":"Revocation and mandatory offenses","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01","sec03-F07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Revocation is the most serious loss, because it ends the license and forces you to start over.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Some offenses leave the Director no choice, so knowing them shows which mistakes are unforgivable.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F09"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Morgan is convicted a second time for driving under the influence of alcohol.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R03"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A second or later conviction for driving under the influence makes revocation mandatory.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R03"]},"result":{"text":"Morgan's license is revoked, and when the period ends Morgan must apply again and pass the complete examinations.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F06"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a revoked license is simply handed back when the period ends.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"After revocation you apply for a new license and must take and pass the complete examinations again.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Revoked means starting over from the test.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver injures someone in a crash and leaves without stopping or giving aid. What happens to the license?","fact_ids":["sec03-F09"]},"answer":{"text":"It must be revoked.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09"]},"rationale":{"text":"Failing to stop, give aid or identify yourself after a crash that injures or kills someone is a mandatory revocation offense.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"The most serious loss","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Revocation ends the license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},{"text":"Some offenses require it.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Revocation is the heaviest action against a driver license, and this lesson explains why. When a license is revoked, it is not simply put on hold. Once the revocation period ends, the driver may apply for a new license, but must take and pass the complete examinations again, just like a beginner. We will also go through the offenses that make revocation mandatory, meaning the Director must revoke. These include crimes committed with a vehicle, repeat impaired driving, leaving an injury crash, and a few others that involve dishonesty or a pattern of recklessness.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Starting over after revocation","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Apply for a new license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]},{"text":"Pass the complete examinations again.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"After a revocation period ends, getting back on the road is not automatic. You may apply for a new license, but you must take and pass the complete examinations again. That is a key difference from cancellation, where the problem is that you were never entitled to the license at all. With revocation, the license was valid until an offense ended it, and you earn it back by testing again from the beginning. Keep that phrase in mind: revoked means apply again and pass every examination, not simply pay a fee and collect the old card.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Crimes that force revocation","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vehicle manslaughter or homicide.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F09"]},{"text":"Using a vehicle for a felony.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"The Director must revoke a license after a conviction for manslaughter or homicide caused by operating a motor vehicle. The same is true when a motor vehicle is used to commit a felony. Failing to stop, give aid, or identify yourself after a crash that kills or injures another person is also a mandatory revocation offense. In each case the vehicle was part of a serious harm, and the law takes away the license as a matter of course. These are not cases where a hearing officer weighs points; the revocation is required once the conviction exists.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07","sec03-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Impaired, dishonest or reckless","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Second impaired-driving conviction.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F10"]},{"text":"Perjury, three reckless convictions, vehicle misuse.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Revocation is also mandatory on a second or later conviction for driving, or being in actual physical control of a vehicle, under the influence of alcohol. The same applies to driving as a habitual user of a controlled substance, or while too impaired by one to drive safely. Three more offenses complete the list: perjury or a false sworn statement to the Director about license or vehicle laws, three reckless driving convictions within twelve months, and the unauthorized use of someone else's vehicle. Each of these requires revocation once the conviction is in place.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"First offense versus repeat","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F08","sec03-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"First DUI: a suspension ground.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F08","sec03-F18"]},{"text":"Second or later: mandatory revocation.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F08","sec03-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"This is the classic trap in the chapter. Many people think any conviction for driving under the influence means revocation. In fact, mandatory revocation is triggered by a second or subsequent conviction, and the same holds for controlled-substance impairment. A first-offense DUI or drug offense appears instead on the list of grounds for suspension. So the count of convictions matters. If a question says first conviction, the answer points toward suspension; if it says second or later, revocation is mandatory and the driver will later need to pass every examination again.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F08","sec03-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a crash scenario","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Injury crash, driver leaves: what follows?","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver injures someone in a crash and leaves without stopping, giving aid or identifying themselves. What happens to the license? Decide before you hear it. The answer is that the license must be revoked. Failing to stop, give aid, or identify yourself after a crash that kills or injures another person is on the list of mandatory revocation offenses. Points or a suspension would not be the right answer here. Once revoked, the driver would have to apply for a new license and pass the complete examinations to drive again.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Revocation in summary","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Mandatory list: harm, repeat DUI, lies.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R03"]},{"text":"Afterward: apply and retest.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, revocation ends the license, and afterward you must apply again and pass the complete examinations, unlike a cancellation, which is about never having been entitled to the license. Revocation is mandatory for manslaughter or homicide by motor vehicle, using a vehicle in a felony, a second or later impaired-driving conviction, leaving a crash that kills or injures someone, perjury or false sworn statements to the Director, three reckless driving convictions within twelve months, and unauthorized use of another person's vehicle. A first impaired conviction is a suspension ground instead.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F09","sec03-F10","sec03-R01","sec03-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u03","module_id":"sec03-m03","objective_ids":["sec03-u03"],"title":{"text":"Grounds for suspension","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02","sec03-F12"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Suspension grounds cover far more than crashes, so ordinary habits like ignoring a summons can cost the license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F14"]},{"text":"Young drivers face extra grounds, so teens and parents need to know them early.","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Riley, seventeen, holds a Graduated Driver License and has just received a second moving violation.","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R10"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Two or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License is on the suspension list, separate from the four-point ground.","fact_ids":["sec03-F17","sec03-R10"]},"result":{"text":"Riley's license can be suspended for the violations, even though Riley may have fewer than four points.","fact_ids":["sec03-R10","sec03-F17"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a suspended license always needs new examinations to come back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]},"correction":{"text":"A suspended license is reinstated after the suspension unless it expired meanwhile or the requirements were not all met.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Suspended comes back; revoked starts over.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F11"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver's license is suspended and expires before the suspension ends. Is it simply reinstated?","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F11"]},"answer":{"text":"No, an expired license is one of the exceptions to reinstatement.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F11"]},"rationale":{"text":"Reinstatement after suspension happens unless the license expired during the suspension or not all requirements were met.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Why licenses get suspended","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Suspension is temporary.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F17"]},{"text":"The grounds list is long.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Suspension is the most common way to lose a license for a while, and the list of reasons is long. In this lesson you will see how suspension differs from revocation, and then the many grounds for it, grouped so they are easier to remember: problems with your driving record, misuse of the license itself, failing legal duties such as answering a summons or keeping required insurance, and special rules for young drivers, including the Graduated Driver License. Several of these surprise new drivers, because they have little to do with how well you steer.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"How suspension works","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Suspended after convictions or incompetence.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Reinstated afterward, with two exceptions.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"A license may be suspended after certain convictions or after a finding that the driver is incompetent to drive. Unlike revocation, a suspension is normally followed by reinstatement. The license comes back after the suspension, unless it expired during that time or the driver did not meet all of the suspension requirements. So a suspension is a time out with conditions. If you let the license expire while it is suspended, or skip a required step, reinstatement does not simply happen, and you will have more to do before you can drive again legally.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Record and license misuse","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Frequent serious violations; reckless record.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},{"text":"Lending, mutilating or out-of-state offenses.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Your driving record can lead to suspension. The grounds include convictions for serious moving violations frequent enough to show disrespect for traffic laws, a record of habitually reckless or negligent driving, and incompetence to drive. Misusing the license itself is another path. Allowing unlawful or fraudulent use of your license, mutilating it, or committing an offense in another state that would be grounds here can all lead to suspension. So the card is not just yours to treat as you like; letting someone else use it can cost you the right to drive.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Legal duties you must meet","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F16","sec03-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fleeing police, racing, ignoring a summons.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F16","sec03-F18"]},{"text":"SR insurance, child support, medical reasons.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F16","sec03-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some grounds are about legal duties. Convictions for fleeing or trying to elude a police officer, or for racing on highways, can bring suspension. So can failing to answer a traffic summons on time or failing to pay. Failing to keep SR-twenty-two insurance when it is required, owing unpaid child support, and medical reasons are further grounds. A first-offense DUI or drug offense, for a juvenile or an adult, is also listed. Notice how many of these come from ignoring paperwork or obligations rather than from a single dangerous moment behind the wheel.","fact_ids":["sec03-F14","sec03-F16","sec03-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Rules for young drivers","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ages fifteen through eighteen leaving school.","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},{"text":"Two violations on a graduated license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Young drivers face extra grounds. Drivers aged fifteen through eighteen who withdraw from school before graduating can, under certain conditions, have the license suspended. The suspension list also includes two or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License. That same list names four or more points on the driving record as a separate ground. For a teen, this means a second moving violation on a graduated license can be enough for suspension even before the point total gets high, so careful driving in the first years matters a great deal.","fact_ids":["sec03-F15","sec03-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two thresholds, two rules","fact_ids":["sec03-R10","sec03-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four or more points on the record.","fact_ids":["sec03-R10","sec03-F17"]},{"text":"Two moving violations on a graduated license.","fact_ids":["sec03-R10","sec03-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. The suspension list names two separate grounds: four or more points on the driving record, and two or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License. They are not the same rule, and neither one is the same as the point schedule you will meet in the next lesson, which starts at twelve points within two years. So learn each number in its own setting. Four points belongs to the suspension list, two violations belongs to graduated licenses, and twelve points is where the point-suspension schedule begins.","fact_ids":["sec03-R10","sec03-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check reinstatement","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Suspended and expired: reinstated?","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver's license is suspended, and it expires before the suspension ends. Is it simply reinstated when the suspension is over? Decide first. The answer is no. A suspended license is reinstated afterward unless it expired during the suspension or the driver did not meet all the suspension requirements, and expiring is one of those exceptions. The driver will have more to do before driving again. Compare that with revocation, where the driver must always apply for a new license and pass the complete examinations, whatever the dates.","fact_ids":["sec03-R02","sec03-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Suspension grounds recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F16","sec03-F17","sec03-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"Record, misuse, duties, young drivers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F16","sec03-F17","sec03-F18"]},{"text":"Usually reinstated afterward.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F16","sec03-F17","sec03-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, a suspension is normally followed by reinstatement, unless the license expired meanwhile or the requirements were not met. The grounds include frequent serious violations, a habitually reckless or negligent record, incompetence, misuse or mutilation of the license, out-of-state offenses, fleeing police, racing, ignoring a summons or not paying, missing required SR insurance, unpaid child support, medical reasons, and a first-offense DUI or drug offense. Young drivers can also lose a license for leaving school, and the list names four points or two graduated-license violations as separate grounds.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-F13","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-F16","sec03-F17","sec03-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u04","module_id":"sec03-m04","objective_ids":["sec03-u04"],"title":{"text":"How many points each offense","fact_ids":["sec03-F19","sec03-F20","sec03-F21"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Points add up across offenses and states, so each ticket moves you closer to a
